Re: Internal Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination  
Member: Reese Delgado  
Member ID: W746473340  
Reference number: POC-13C871BB40-43334  
Requested service: Lumbar decompression/disc surgery  
CPT code: 63030  
Date of denial: August 14, 2026

To the Appeals Department:

I request reversal of the denial and authorization of CPT 63030, lumbar decompression/disc surgery, as recommended by Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgeon.

The denial identified insufficient conservative treatment as the reason for nonauthorization. The clinical record demonstrates an extensive and unsuccessful course of nonoperative treatment:

- I have experienced nine months of progressive lower-back pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- I completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy from April 11, 2026, through July 18, 2026, including core stabilization and lumbar-flexibility treatment. The physical-therapy discharge note documents 16 completed visits.
- I used NSAIDs for six months without adequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on May 23, 2026. It provided only three weeks of partial relief.
- Despite these measures, I remain unable to stand for more than 10 minutes and continue to experience radicular pain extending into the right calf.

The medical records also establish a specific structural and neurologic cause for the persistent symptoms. A lumbar MRI performed on June 22, 2026, showed an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral-recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. Examination documented positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.

Accordingly, this is not a request based solely on nonspecific back pain. The records show persistent disabling symptoms, failure of prolonged supervised therapy and medication, only temporary and incomplete response to injection treatment, objective MRI-confirmed nerve-root compression, and corresponding neurologic findings. CPT 63030 is being requested to address the documented L4-L5 pathology and L5 nerve-root compression.

The publicly available materials reviewed for this appeal did not establish which specific medical policy, clinical-utilization guideline, version, or criteria were applied to this determination. I therefore have not quoted or attributed any medical-necessity language to the plan. Please provide the exact criteria used for this review, including the applicable document title, policy or guideline number, version, effective date, and the specific conservative-treatment requirement applied to CPT 63030.

Please reconsider the denial based on the enclosed documentation and authorize the requested surgery. If Anthem maintains the denial, please provide a written explanation identifying each unmet criterion, the clinical basis for that conclusion, the records considered, and the applicable appeal and external-review rights.

Please accept this appeal as timely. The denial notice states that the appeal must be received by February 10, 2027.

Enclosures:

1. August 14, 2026 adverse benefit determination  
2. Physical-therapy discharge note documenting 14 weeks of treatment and 16 completed visits  
3. Medication-treatment history documenting six months of NSAID use  
4. Injection record from May 23, 2026  
5. Lumbar MRI report dated June 22, 2026  
6. Examination findings documenting positive provocative testing and the corresponding neurologic deficit  
7. Operative recommendation from Okafor, MD  
8. Any additional clinical records supporting medical necessity

Sincerely,

Reese Delgado
